'''''Goeppertia insignis''''' (syn. ''Calathea lancifolia'', ''Goeppertia lancifolia''), the '''rattlesnake plant''', is a species of flowering plant in the [[Marantaceae]] [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[native plant|native]] to [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro state]] in Brazil.<ref name="77174285-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77174285-1 |title=''Goeppertia insignis'' (W.Bull ex W.E.Marshall) J.M.A.Braga, L.J.T.Cardoso & R.Couto |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=12 May 2021 }}</ref>  

It is an [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing to {{cvt|60|-|75|cm|0}}, with slender pale green leaves to {{cvt|45|cm|0}}, heavily marked above with dark blotches, purple below.<ref>{{cite book |title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants |year=2008 |publisher=Dorling Kindersley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1405332965 |pages=1136}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=''Calathea lancifolia'' rattlesnake plant |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/2628/calathea-lancifolia/details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=12 May 2021 }}</ref>

In the Peruvian Amazon, the plant is used for wrapping brown sugar.<ref name="AED">{{cite book |last1=Duke |first1=James A. |last2=Vasquez |first2=Rodolfo |title=Amazonian Ethnobotanical Dictionary |date=1994 |publisher=CRC Press |page=36}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
''Goeppertia insignis'' prefers indirect sunlight.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=''Goeppertia insignis'' {{!}} rattlesnake plant/RHS Gardening |url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/386634/Goeppertia-insignis/Details |access-date=2020-09-17 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> These plants want well-drained, but moist, soil.<ref name=":0" /> They like a pH of 6.1 to 7.3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plant database entry for Rattlesnake Plant (''Goeppertia lancifolia'') with 25 images and 23 data details. |url=https://garden.org/plants/view/240101/Rattlesnake-Plant-Goeppertia-lancifolia |access-date=2020-09-17 |website=garden.org |language=en}}</ref> The plant requires a minimum temperature of {{cvt|16|C}}, and it is commonly used as a [[houseplant]] in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions.

== Leaves ==
The bottom side of the leaves are purple, with the adaxial surface having what look like dark green alternating large and small [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]] overlaid on the light green leaf.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Goeppertia insignis'' (''Calathea lancifolia'' 2, Prayer Plant, Rattlesnake Calathea, Rattlesnake Master, Rattlesnake Plant) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/goeppertia-insignis |access-date=2020-09-17 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref> Like other prayer plants, its leaves fold together at night, and unfold again in the morning.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prayer Plant - ''Maranta leuconeura'' Picture, Care Tips |url=https://www.guide-to-houseplants.com/prayer-plant.html |access-date=2020-09-18 |website=www.guide-to-houseplants.com}}</ref>
